decision_description: Conflict between the constitution (CLAUDE.md §8.1/§8.4, C1 amendment — authority level 2) and the Tier 4 Phase 7 output docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json (authority level 7) over the budget-gate outcome for this MSCA-PF run. The Tier 4 assessment executed lump-sum interface validation (Mode B), halted at Step B.1.1 because docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/ holds only a .gitkeep, and declared gate_pass_declaration=fail (BLK-01). In the same phase, docs/.../phase7_budget_gate/unit_cost_budget.json derives the budget deterministically for the MSCA-PF unit-cost regime (total EUR 220723.50; 30 confirmed months x published rates x HU host coefficient 78.7%), with every line_item status=Confirmed, unresolved_components=[] and blocking_inconsistencies=[], and declares gate_pass_declaration=pass. The specific issue: which budget source governs gate_09 for a unit-cost instrument. The C1 amendment establishes that the external Lump Sum Budget Planner 'received/' requirement is the exclusive source for lump-sum instruments ONLY; for unit-cost instruments (MSCA-PF) the sole sanctioned source is the internal deterministic derivation (§8.1). The lump-sum Mode B assessment therefore applied an inapplicable validation mode to a unit-cost instrument. Resolution: the constitution (level 2) governs over the Tier 4 phase output (level 7) by subordination; the budget gate for this run is resolved against the unit_cost_budget.json deterministic derivation, whose components are all Confirmed with no unresolved or blocking items. The lump-sum budget_gate_assessment.json fail is recorded as a mode misapplication and must not be used to block Phase 8 for this unit-cost run; it should be re-run in unit-cost mode or superseded by the unit-cost derivation.
alternatives_considered: Accept the Tier 4 budget_gate_assessment.json fail (BLK-01) at face value and treat Phase 8 as blocked — rejected: this applies the lump-sum-only external-'received/' requirement to a unit-cost MSCA-PF instrument, contrary to the C1 amendment to §8.1/§8.4, which scopes 'exclusively external' to lump-sum instruments and designates the internal deterministic derivation as the sole sanctioned source for unit-cost.

Log the divergence as an unresolved conflict and escalate to the operator per CLAUDE.md §3 — rejected: the conflict is resolvable by subordination (constitution, authority level 2, governs Tier 4 orchestration state, authority level 7), so §3 unresolved-escalation is not triggered.

Generate or substitute a lump-sum budget response internally to satisfy the 'received/' requirement — rejected as a categorical anti-fabrication violation under §8.3/§13.3, and unnecessary because the unit-cost regime does not use the Lump Sum Budget Planner integration.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §8.1 and §8.4 (C1 Amendment — instrument-conditional budget gate: unit-cost derivation is the sanctioned source for unit-cost instruments; external lump-sum 'received/' response required only for lump-sum instruments); CLAUDE.md §3 authority hierarchy — the constitution (authority level 2) governs over Tier 4 orchestration state (authority level 7, docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json), which is the subordinate source in this conflict.
rationale: The instrument for this run is MSCA-PF (unit_cost regime), confirmed in unit_cost_budget.json (instrument_type=MSCA-PF, budget_regime=unit_cost) and consistent with selected_call.json. Under the C1 amendment to §8.1/§8.4, unit-cost budgets carry no judgment and are byte-equal replay-verifiable, so deterministic derivation supplies the anti-fabrication guarantee that externalisation supplies for lump-sum; consequently the external Lump Sum Budget Planner is neither required nor applicable for a unit-cost instrument. The budget_gate_assessment.json failure arises solely from running lump-sum Mode B validation (checking the empty received/ directory), which is the wrong validation mode for this instrument, not from any deficiency in the budget itself. The applicable source — unit_cost_budget.json — satisfies the categorical, instrument-independent §8.4 gate condition: every budget component, including the sole host-dependent line (living_allowance), is resolved to Confirmed, with unresolved_components=[] and blocking_inconsistencies=[]. Because the conflict is between the constitution (level 2) and a Tier 4 phase output (level 7), it is resolved by subordination in favour of the constitution rather than escalated as unresolved. This decision documents an interpretation only; it does not write a gate_result artifact (gate evaluation remains the scheduler's exclusive responsibility per §17.6.2). Recording this in Tier 4 is mandatory per §9.4, §12.3 and §13.5 so the mode-misapplication and its resolution are durable and auditable rather than held only in agent memory.
